title: Quantitative Characterization of Peripheral Soil Geochemical Zoning in a Porphyry Mineral System and Implications for Mineral Exploration: A Case Study of Ganlongla on the Northern Margin of the Giant Yulong Copper Deposit, Tibet
content: The peripheries of porphyry mineral systems offer important opportunities for exploration at depth and in adjacent areas. Conventional soil geochemical interpretation, however, relies largely on single-element concentration classes and provides limited constraints on whether an anomaly represents a proximal, high-temperature core or a distal frontal halo. This study examines analytical data for 16 elements from 1,325 surface-soil samples collected in the Ganlongla area, north of the giant Yulong porphyry-skarn Cu (Mo, Au) deposit in Tibet. Element background concentrations and anomaly thresholds were estimated using an iterative lognormal procedure, and element associations were identified using correlation analysis, R-mode cluster analysis, and orthogonally rotated factor analysis. Drawing on the concept of primary-halo zoning in hydrothermal deposits, four composite log-contrast indices were developed for the inner zone (Cu-Mo-W-Bi), contact zone (Cu-Au-Ag), peripheral zone (Pb-Zn-Ag-As-Sb-Hg), and skarn association (W-Bi). A zoning index, ZI, defined as the peripheral-zone index minus the inner-zone index, was then used to quantify the position of each sampling site relative to the mineralization center. Density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN) was subsequently used to delineate anomaly clusters and rank exploration targets. The high-temperature and skarn associations show their highest contrast values in the south and decline systematically northward, whereas ZI increases monotonically from south to north, from 0.143 to 0.293, with a slope of approximately 9.73 × 10⁻⁵ m⁻¹. These patterns are consistent with the main Yulong orebody lying south of the survey area and Ganlongla occupying its northern outer contact zone and periphery. Three Class A, two Class B, and two Class C targets were delineated, together with an isolated, exceptionally strong anomaly requiring field verification. This composite contrast-index and zoning-index approach provides a reproducible quantitative basis for advancing peripheral soil geochemical exploration in covered porphyry mineral systems from anomaly detection toward assessment of relative position and depth within the system.
